steps.title: Launch Anvi'o via Docker
steps.instruction: If the Anvi'o commands are not found, run them inside the official Docker image.

substeps.instruction: Move the downloaded files to a new folder inside your Documents (e.g., ~/Documents/anvio_workdir).
Open a Docker quick‑start terminal and cd to that folder; run pwd to obtain the absolute path (e.g., /c/Users/yourname/Documents/anvio_workdir).
Start the Anvi'o container, mounting the folder as /my_data and exposing port 8080:
If a previous container is still running, list containers with docker ps and terminate the offending one with docker kill <container_id>.

steps.title: Create contigs database
steps.instruction: Inside the Docker container (or on a native installation), generate a contigs database from contigs.fa:

substeps.instruction: Note: the command computes k‑mer frequencies (default k‑mer size = 4) and splits contigs longer than 20,000 kbp (default) into smaller pieces; you can change these with --kmer-size <size> and --split-length <bp>.
To skip mindful splitting for very large assemblies, add --skip-mindful-splitting.
Gene calling is performed with Prodigal by default; to skip it, add --skip-gene-calling, or to supply your own calls, add --external-gene-calls <file>.

steps.title: Annotate contigs with HMMs
steps.instruction: Run the built‑in HMM search to annotate single‑copy core genes in the contigs database.

substeps.instruction: By default the command uses one CPU; to speed up the run, add --num-threads <N> where N is the number of cores you wish to use.
To add custom HMM profiles, place them in a directory and specify it with --hmm-profile-dir <path>.
